found.desc: Gospels of Landévennec: animal representation of the Evangelist St. Matthew (from the Bodleian Library, Oxford, copy from the now ruined Landévennec Abbey in Brittany, France). Housed in a semicircular arch, the evangelist sat holds in his hands the two instruments necessary for the writing of the manuscript: the calamus (piece of cut reed) in his right hand, and in the other a scraper. Matthew is represented with a human head and an animal body, not like the other three evangelists. In the Bodleian Library, University of Oxford, Oxford, England.

found.title: File:Cottages and monastery, Caldey Island - geograph.org.uk - 590728.jpg
found.desc: Cottages and monastery, Caldey Island The cottages were built in the early 19C, but remodelled by John Coates Carter in the first decade of the 20C. The monastery was initially Anglo-Catholic, established in 1900 although it was 1906 before they could start building here. The founder was Benjamin Fearnley Carlyle, an Anglican Benedictine. The island was purchased from William Done Bushell, a senior master at Harrow who had bought it as a holiday home in 1897. The monastery has a Continental appearance, but the large arches to the basement show the influence of the American architect H H Richar
